title: Factory-Capacity Notices Before a Hold Release and Capacity Resequencing
content:
Factory-capacity delay notices on the order decide capacity resequencing. For Factory Production Orders, capacity resequencing adds business days at a hold's release by the factory-capacity delay notices recorded on the order less than three whole calendar months before the release date (a notice dated three or more whole months before it does not count):

- **two or more** such notices add **3 business days**;
- **one** adds **2 business days**;
- none adds nothing.

The days added are counted in business days (Monday through Friday, excluding U.S. federal holidays) starting the day after the ship date first set at release, and the date reached is the requoted ship date.

## Which notices count

Only delay notices with cause factory capacity on the order's own milestone records are counted, each by its date. Notices of other causes — glass supplier, weather and freight, customer hold, late acknowledgment, customer specification remake — are not counted here.

## The three-month line (hypothetical release on 15 June)

| Notice date | Whole calendar months before the release | Counts |
|---|---|---|
| 20 May | under one | yes |
| 16 March | two whole months, not three | yes |
| 15 March | three | no |
| 2 February | four | no |

## Hypothetical cases

- Factory-capacity notices dated 10 April and 1 June, release on 15 June: two notices count, 3 business days.
- Factory-capacity notices dated 1 January and 1 June, release on 15 June: only the June notice counts, 2 business days.
